q: Which of the following is an example of contingent expenditure?

options.A: Petty office expenses such as postage, stationery and similar incidental charges
options.B: The cost of constructing a new station building
options.C: Liquidated damages recovered from a contractor
options.D: Salary of regular establishment

e: Contingent expenditure covers petty and incidental office expenses such as postage, stationery and similar charges, as distinct from works expenditure or salary of the regular establishment.

q: In the two-packet system of tendering:

options.A: The technical and financial bids are opened simultaneously for all tenderers
options.B: The financial packet is opened first and the technical packet later
options.C: Two separate contracts are awarded for one work
options.D: The financial packets of only those tenderers whose technical/eligibility packets are found acceptable are opened

e: In the two-packet system, the financial packets of only those tenderers whose technical or eligibility packets are found acceptable are opened, so that price does not influence the technical evaluation.

q: In works tenders, the Earnest Money Deposit required from tenderers is subject to a maximum (cap) of:

options.A: Rs 10 lakh
options.B: Rs 25 lakh
options.C: Rs 50 lakh
options.D: Rs 2 crore

e: The Earnest Money Deposit required from tenderers in works tenders is subject to a maximum cap of Rs 50 lakh, so that the earnest money does not grow disproportionately for very large tenders.

q: Tenders for a work are opened:

options.A: At the appointed date and time, in the presence of such tenderers or their authorised representatives as choose to be present
options.B: Only after the tender committee submits its report
options.C: In the office of the contractor who is expected to be the lowest
options.D: After the Letter of Acceptance is issued

e: Tenders for a work are opened at the appointed date and time in the presence of such tenderers or their authorised representatives as choose to be present, ensuring transparency of the opening process.

q: If the acceptance of a tender is not communicated to the tenderer within the validity period of his tender:

options.A: The tender is deemed to have been accepted automatically
options.B: The tenderer is no longer bound by his offer and may withdraw it without forfeiture of the earnest money
options.C: The earnest money is automatically forfeited
options.D: The validity is deemed to be extended indefinitely

e: If acceptance of a tender is not communicated within the validity period of the tender, the tenderer is no longer bound by his offer and may withdraw it without forfeiture of the earnest money.

q: As per the Government e-Marketplace provisions in the General Financial Rules, goods and services available on GeM:

options.A: Can be procured only through open tenders
options.B: Are procured by the Railways only from registered agents
options.C: Cannot be procured by the Railways at all
options.D: Are required to be procured through GeM itself by the government buyers

e: As per the GeM provisions in the General Financial Rules, goods and services available on GeM are required to be procured through GeM itself by the government buyers.

q: Arbitration proceedings for disputes arising out of railway works contracts are governed by:

options.A: The Indian Contract Act, 1872
options.B: The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
options.C: The Railways Act, 1989
options.D: The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908

e: Arbitration proceedings for disputes arising out of railway works contracts are governed by the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, which regulates the appointment of arbitrators, the proceedings and the award.

q: The measurements recorded in a Measurement Book by an official are required to be:

options.A: Test-checked by his superior officer to the extent prescribed
options.B: Accepted without any check in all cases
options.C: Checked only by the contractor
options.D: Checked only after the final bill is paid

e: The measurements recorded in a Measurement Book by an official are required to be test-checked by his superior officer to the extent prescribed, so that correctness of measurements is ensured before payment.

q: The final bill of a works contract is:

options.A: The first running bill of the contractor
options.B: A bill for extra items only
options.C: Prepared before the commencement of the work
options.D: Prepared on completion of the work for the total value of the work done, after adjusting all the on-account payments already made to the contractor

e: The final bill is prepared on completion of the work for the total value of the work done, after adjusting all the on-account payments already made to the contractor, to arrive at the balance payable.

q: The electronic Measurement Book (e-MB) for works contracts is maintained on:

options.A: IREPS
options.B: IPAS
options.C: IRWCMS (Indian Railways Works Contract Management System)
options.D: FOIS

e: The electronic Measurement Book (e-MB) for works contracts is maintained on IRWCMS, the Indian Railways Works Contract Management System.

q: In a works contract, the 'Engineer' means:

options.A: Any engineer employed by the contractor
options.B: The officer designated in the contract under whose supervision and direction the work is to be executed
options.C: The Chief Engineer of the Railway Board
options.D: The engineer who prepared the abstract estimate

e: In a works contract, the Engineer means the officer designated in the contract under whose supervision and direction the work is to be executed by the contractor.

q: The maintenance/defect liability period of a completed work normally runs from:

options.A: The date of issue of the completion certificate for the work
options.B: The date of opening of tenders
options.C: The date of the first running bill
options.D: The date of sanction of the detailed estimate

e: The maintenance or defect liability period of a completed work normally runs from the date of issue of the completion certificate for the work, during which defects appearing are rectified by the contractor.

q: Amounts due to the Railway from a contractor, such as the cost of departmental materials supplied to him and hire charges of tools and plant, are ordinarily recovered:

options.A: Only through a civil suit
options.B: From the contractor's earnest money deposit
options.C: After the expiry of ten years
options.D: From the running (on-account) bills payable to the contractor

e: Amounts due to the Railway from a contractor, such as the cost of departmental materials supplied to him and hire charges of tools and plant, are ordinarily recovered from the running or on-account bills payable to him.

q: Expenditure on ordinary repairs and maintenance of existing railway assets is charged to:

options.A: Capital
options.B: The Capital Fund
options.C: Revenue (working expenses)
options.D: The Depreciation Reserve Fund in all cases

e: Expenditure on ordinary repairs and maintenance of existing railway assets merely keeps them in working order and creates no new asset, so it is charged to Revenue as working expenses.

q: In a percentage-rate contract, the contractor:

options.A: Quotes a separate rate for each item of work
options.B: Quotes a single percentage above or below the schedule of rates at which he agrees to execute the work
options.C: Is paid a fixed lump sum for the whole work
options.D: Is paid on a cost-plus-fee basis only

e: In a percentage-rate contract, the contractor quotes a single percentage above or below the schedule of rates at which he agrees to execute the work, instead of quoting separate rates for each item.

q: Under the General Conditions of Contract, a contractor:

options.A: Cannot sublet or assign the work, or any part of it, to another party without the prior written consent of the Railway
options.B: Is free to sublet the entire work to any other contractor
options.C: Can assign the contract to his creditors at his discretion
options.D: Can sublet the work after merely informing the sectional staff

e: Under the GCC, a contractor cannot sublet or assign the work, or any part of it, to another party without the prior written consent of the Railway, since the contract is awarded on his own credentials.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Deviations from the sanctioned provisions of a contract, beyond the limits laid down, require the sanction of the competent authority.
2. A contractor may execute extra items on his own, without the orders of the Engineer, and claim payment for them as a matter of right.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: deviations beyond the limits laid down require the sanction of the competent authority. Statement 2 is false: a contractor cannot execute extra items on his own, without the Engineer's orders, and claim payment as a matter of right.

q: A 'token' provision made against a work in the budget (Pink Book) signifies that:

options.A: The work has been dropped from the Works Programme
options.B: The full cost of the work will be spent in that year itself
options.C: The work is to be executed free of cost to the Railways
options.D: The work is an approved work for which only a nominal allotment is made in that year, the bulk of the funds being provided in later years as the work progresses

e: A token provision against a work in the Pink Book signifies that the work is an approved work for which only a nominal allotment is made in that year, the bulk of the funds being provided in later years as the work progresses.

q: Measurements of work which will subsequently be covered up, such as foundations below ground, should be:

options.A: Recorded after the covering work is completed
options.B: Estimated approximately at the time of the final bill
options.C: Recorded in the Measurement Book before the work is covered up
options.D: Recorded only if the contractor so demands

e: Measurements of work which will subsequently be covered up, such as foundations below ground, should be recorded in the Measurement Book before the work is covered up, since they cannot be verified afterwards.

q: The issue of the Letter of Acceptance to the successful tenderer:

options.A: Is a mere formality with no legal effect
options.B: Communicates the acceptance of his tender and brings the contract into existence, even before the formal agreement is executed
options.C: Replaces the need for security deposit in all cases
options.D: Entitles the contractor to payment in advance for the whole work

e: The issue of the Letter of Acceptance communicates the acceptance of the successful tenderer's tender and brings the contract into existence, even before the formal agreement is executed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure which creates a new asset, or substantially adds to the capacity of an existing asset, is charged to Capital or the appropriate capital fund head.
2. Expenditure which merely maintains an existing asset in working order, without adding to its capacity, is charged to Revenue.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: expenditure which creates a new asset or substantially adds to the capacity of an existing asset is charged to Capital or the appropriate capital fund head, while expenditure which merely maintains an asset in working order is charged to Revenue.

q: When an existing asset is renewed and, at the same time, improved to a higher standard, the cost of the work is:

options.A: Charged wholly to Capital in all cases
options.B: Apportioned, the cost of like-for-like renewal being charged to the renewal head (such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund) and the additional cost of the improvement to the appropriate capital head
options.C: Charged wholly to Revenue
options.D: Recovered from the contractor executing the renewal

e: When an asset is renewed and improved at the same time, the cost is apportioned: the cost of like-for-like renewal is charged to the renewal head such as DRF, and the additional cost of the improvement to the appropriate capital head.

q: The cost of surveys and investigations carried out for a proposed work which is finally abandoned and not executed is:

options.A: Kept under a suspense head indefinitely
options.B: Charged to Capital
options.C: Recovered from the agency which conducted the survey
options.D: Written off to Revenue

e: The cost of surveys and investigations for a proposed work which is finally abandoned creates no asset, so it is written off to Revenue rather than remaining charged to Capital.

q: Minor works on the Railways are works which:

options.A: Are charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund in all cases
options.B: Cost less than the prescribed monetary limit and are charged to Revenue
options.C: Are individually sanctioned by the Railway Board
options.D: Can be executed only by the Railway Board's own agencies

e: Minor works are works costing less than the prescribed monetary limit and charged to Revenue; they are sanctioned against the lump-sum provision made for minor works and not individually by the Railway Board.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A lump-sum provision for minor works is made in the Works Programme, and individual minor works are sanctioned against it during the year.
2. Every minor work is individually listed in the Pink Book and is sanctioned by the Railway Board.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: a lump-sum provision for minor works is made in the Works Programme and individual minor works are sanctioned against it during the year. Statement 2 is false, as minor works are neither individually listed in the Pink Book nor sanctioned by the Railway Board.

q: Works intended primarily for passenger amenities and staff welfare are generally financed from:

options.A: Capital
options.B: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: The Development Fund
options.D: The Railway Safety Fund

e: Works intended primarily for passenger amenities and staff welfare are generally financed from the Development Fund, which is provided for improvement works of this nature on the Railways.

q: The Preliminary Works Programme (PWP) is:

options.A: The final list of works sanctioned by Parliament for the year
options.B: A register of completed works maintained by the divisions
options.C: A list of the expenditure heads appearing in the budget
options.D: The preliminary list of works proposed by the Zonal Railways and submitted to the Railway Board for selection of works for inclusion in the Works Programme

e: The Preliminary Works Programme (PWP) is the preliminary list of works proposed by the Zonal Railways and submitted to the Railway Board for selection of works for inclusion in the Works Programme.

q: Inclusion of a work in the Pink Book (Works Programme) means that:

options.A: The detailed estimate of the work stands automatically sanctioned
options.B: The work forms part of the approved programme, but expenditure on it can be incurred only after its estimate is sanctioned by the competent authority
options.C: Funds for the work can be drawn without sanction of any estimate
options.D: The work must necessarily be completed within that financial year

e: Inclusion of a work in the Pink Book means the work forms part of the approved programme, but expenditure on it can be incurred only after its estimate is sanctioned by the competent authority.

q: In the Works Programme, works are arranged under Plan Heads. Track renewal works are classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 11
options.B: Plan Head 21
options.C: Plan Head 31
options.D: Plan Head 51

e: In the Works Programme, works are arranged under Plan Heads, and track renewal works are classified under Plan Head 31.

q: The LAW Book (List of Approved Works) shows, in respect of each approved work:

options.A: The anticipated or sanctioned cost of the work and the allotment provided for it for the year
options.B: Only the name of the contractor executing the work
options.C: The measurements of the work done from time to time
options.D: The audit objections outstanding against the work

e: The LAW Book shows, in respect of each approved work, the anticipated or sanctioned cost of the work and the allotment provided for it for the year.

q: A work which is not included in the sanctioned Works Programme may be taken up 'out of turn' when:

options.A: The contractor executing other works in the section requests for it
options.B: The division has spare labour available with it
options.C: The work happens to be a deposit work
options.D: The work is of an urgent nature, such as an urgent safety or restoration work, and is sanctioned by the competent authority within its powers

e: A work not included in the sanctioned Works Programme may be taken up out of turn when it is of an urgent nature, such as an urgent safety or restoration work, and is sanctioned by the competent authority within its powers.

q: Materials issued from a stores depot for use on a work are accounted for by:

options.A: Debiting Stores Suspense and crediting the work
options.B: Debiting the Material-at-Site account of the work and crediting Stores Suspense
options.C: Debiting the personal account of the contractor
options.D: Crediting the Material-at-Site account and debiting Revenue

e: Materials issued from a stores depot for use on a work are accounted for by debiting the Material-at-Site account of the work and crediting Stores Suspense, so that the materials stand charged to the work till consumed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Material-at-Site account of a work is credited as and when the materials are actually consumed on the work.
2. Materials still lying unconsumed at the site on completion of a work are automatically written off as a loss to the work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: the Material-at-Site account is credited as and when the materials are actually consumed on the work. Statement 2 is false, as materials still lying unconsumed on completion are returned to stores or otherwise adjusted, not automatically written off as a loss.

q: Serviceable materials which become surplus on a work and are returned to the stores depot are:

options.A: Treated as scrap in all cases
options.B: Charged to the contractor at penal rates
options.C: Taken back into stock, and the work is given credit for their value
options.D: Written off without any adjustment in the accounts of the work

e: Serviceable materials which become surplus on a work and are returned to the stores depot are taken back into stock, and the work is given credit for their value so that it does not bear their cost.

q: The Material-at-Site balances of works are reconciled by:

options.A: Physical verification of the materials actually lying at the sites of the works
options.B: Comparison with the balances in the contractor's ledger
options.C: Reference to the allotment shown in the Pink Book
options.D: Checking the tender documents of the works

e: The Material-at-Site balances of works are reconciled by physical verification of the materials actually lying at the sites of the works and comparison with the book balances.

q: Expenditure incurred in connection with works, which is recoverable from outside parties, staff or contractors, or which is awaiting adjustment, is initially booked under the suspense head:

options.A: Purchase Suspense
options.B: Traffic Suspense
options.C: Stores Suspense
options.D: Miscellaneous Works Advances

e: Expenditure in connection with works which is recoverable from outside parties, staff or contractors, or which is awaiting adjustment, is initially booked under the suspense head Miscellaneous Works Advances.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A debit balance under Miscellaneous Works Advances represents compensation paid by the Railways to contractors for delay in completion of works.
2. A debit balance under Miscellaneous Works Advances represents amounts outstanding for recovery or adjustment in connection with works.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: a debit balance under Miscellaneous Works Advances is not compensation paid to contractors. Statement 2 is true: it represents amounts outstanding for recovery or adjustment in connection with works.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Balances under suspense heads are expected to be cleared promptly by recovery or adjustment and should not be allowed to remain outstanding for long.
2. Amounts once debited to a suspense head automatically become part of the final cost of the work concerned.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: balances under suspense heads are expected to be cleared promptly by recovery or adjustment and should not remain outstanding for long. Statement 2 is false, as amounts debited to a suspense head do not automatically become part of the final cost of the work.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The contractor is responsible for paying wages to the labour engaged by him, in accordance with the applicable labour laws.
2. If the contractor defaults in paying his labour and the Railway, as principal employer, has to make the payment, the amount so paid can be recovered from the sums due to the contractor.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: the contractor is responsible for paying wages to the labour engaged by him under the applicable labour laws, and if the Railway, as principal employer, has to pay on his default, the amount can be recovered from the sums due to the contractor.

q: Compensation payable for injury to a workman engaged by a contractor on a railway work is, in the first instance, the liability of:

options.A: The Railway Administration
options.B: The State Government
options.C: The workman's trade union
options.D: The contractor, as the employer of the workman

e: Compensation payable for injury to a workman engaged by a contractor is, in the first instance, the liability of the contractor as the employer of the workman.

q: Under the conditions of a works contract, the safety of the workmen at the site, including the provision of protective equipment and safe working arrangements, is the responsibility of:

options.A: The contractor executing the work
options.B: The Railway's safety organisation
options.C: The Labour Inspector of the area
options.D: The tender committee which awarded the work

e: Under the conditions of a works contract, the safety of the workmen at the site, including provision of protective equipment and safe working arrangements, is the responsibility of the contractor executing the work.

q: If, during the execution of a work, damage is caused to railway property or to third parties by the contractor's operations, the liability for such damage rests with:

options.A: The Engineer-in-charge personally
options.B: The Railway in all cases
options.C: The insurance surveyor
options.D: The contractor

e: If damage is caused to railway property or to third parties by the contractor's operations during execution of a work, the liability for such damage rests with the contractor.

q: For major works contracts, the insurance taken by the contractor to cover the work against loss or damage from causes such as fire, flood and accident during execution is known as:

options.A: Marine insurance
options.B: Fidelity insurance
options.C: Contractor's All Risks (CAR) insurance
options.D: Group insurance of labour

e: For major works contracts, the insurance taken by the contractor to cover the work against loss or damage from causes such as fire, flood and accident during execution is known as Contractor's All Risks (CAR) insurance.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The insurance of the works during the period of execution is arranged by the contractor at his own cost.
2. The Railway takes out insurance policies covering the contractor's plant, machinery and labour.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: the insurance of the works during the period of execution is arranged by the contractor at his own cost. Statement 2 is false, as the Railway does not take out policies covering the contractor's plant, machinery and labour.

q: Where a work on railway land is executed by an outside party itself, but under the supervision of the Railway, the Railway recovers from the party:

options.A: Supervision charges, for the supervision exercised by the Railway over the work
options.B: Full departmental charges as are levied on a deposit work
options.C: Liquidated damages for the period of execution
options.D: The full cost of the work as a deposit

e: Where a work on railway land is executed by an outside party itself but under the supervision of the Railway, the Railway recovers supervision charges from the party for the supervision exercised over the work.

q: Departmental charges are leviable:

options.A: Only on works executed for private firms
options.B: Only on works executed for State Governments
options.C: Only when the work is executed outside railway premises
options.D: On works executed by the Railway for other government departments and outside bodies alike, and not merely for private parties

e: Departmental charges are leviable on works executed by the Railway for other government departments and outside bodies alike, and not merely for private parties or only for works outside railway premises.

q: In respect of the amount deposited by a party for the execution of a deposit work:

options.A: Interest is payable by the Railways to the party for the period the amount remains with the Railways
options.B: No interest is payable by the Railways on the amount so deposited
options.C: Interest is payable at the rate applicable to balances in the Public Account
options.D: Interest is adjusted against the departmental charges of the work

e: No interest is payable by the Railways on the amount deposited by a party for execution of a deposit work for the period the amount remains with the Railways.

q: On completion of a deposit work, if the actual cost of the work, including departmental charges, is less than the amount deposited by the party, the balance amount is:

options.A: Forfeited to the Railways
options.B: Retained by the Railways as its earnings
options.C: Refunded to the party
options.D: Transferred to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

e: On completion of a deposit work, if the actual cost of the work including departmental charges is less than the amount deposited by the party, the balance amount is refunded to the party.

q: Where a new road is constructed across an existing railway line, or a new railway line across an existing road, the cost of providing the level crossing or bridge is, as a general principle, borne by:

options.A: The Railways in all cases
options.B: The road authority in all cases
options.C: The authority whose road or line is constructed later and thereby necessitates the crossing
options.D: The Central Government in all cases

e: As a general principle, the cost of providing a level crossing or bridge is borne by the authority whose road or line is constructed later and thereby necessitates the crossing.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a cost-sharing road over-bridge replacing a level crossing, the cost of the bridge structure across the railway tracks is borne by the Railways.
2. The cost of the road approaches to such a bridge is borne by the road authority or the State Government.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: in a cost-sharing road over-bridge replacing a level crossing, the cost of the bridge structure across the railway tracks is borne by the Railways, and the cost of the road approaches is borne by the road authority or the State Government.

q: The capital cost of constructing a private siding for a firm is normally borne by:

options.A: The Railways
options.B: The firm (siding owner) for whom the siding is provided
options.C: The State Government
options.D: The Ministry of Industry

e: A private siding is provided solely for the firm's own traffic and benefit, so the capital cost of constructing it is borne by the firm (siding owner), not by the Railways.

q: An 'assisted siding', as distinguished from an ordinary private siding, is one in which:

options.A: The firm is assisted with a bank loan for constructing the siding
options.B: The Railways maintain the entire siding free of charge
options.C: The siding is constructed by the State Government for the firm
options.D: The Railways bear the cost of that portion of the siding which lies within railway land, as an assistance to the firm

e: In an assisted siding, the Railways share the cost by bearing the cost of the portion lying within railway land, as assistance to the firm; the remaining cost is borne by the firm.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The owner of a private siding pays licence fee for the railway land occupied by the siding, where railway land is used.
2. The owner of a private siding is not required to pay any maintenance charges for the portion of the siding which is maintained by the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: licence fee is payable for railway land occupied by the siding. Statement 2 is wrong: the owner does pay maintenance charges for the portion of the siding maintained by the Railways.

q: In the BOT (Build, Operate and Transfer) model of public-private partnership:

options.A: The private partner only supplies materials for the project
options.B: The Government builds and operates the facility and the private partner only finances it
options.C: The facility remains in the permanent ownership of the private partner
options.D: The private partner builds the facility, operates it during the concession period to recover its investment, and transfers it to the authority at the end of that period

e: Under BOT, the private partner builds the facility, operates it during the concession period to recover its investment, and transfers it to the authority at the end of that period.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the annuity model of public-private partnership, the private partner is paid fixed annuity payments by the authority during the concession period.
2. Under the annuity model, the traffic or revenue risk remains with the authority and not with the private partner.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: under the annuity model the authority pays fixed annuity amounts during the concession period, so the traffic and revenue risk remains with the authority, not with the private partner.

q: Unauthorised occupation (encroachment) of railway land can be got vacated under the provisions of:

options.A: The Indian Contract Act, 1872
options.B: The Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971
options.C: The Land Acquisition Act, 1894
options.D: The Indian Easements Act, 1882

e: Unauthorised occupation of railway land, which is public premises, is got vacated under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971, which provides a summary eviction procedure.

q: The statutory authority set up for the commercial development of vacant railway land is:

options.A: IRCON International Limited
options.B: RITES Limited
options.C: Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA)
options.D: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation

e: The Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA) is the statutory authority set up for the commercial development of vacant railway land and railway air space.

q: A way-leave permission granted over railway land:

options.A: Creates a leasehold interest in favour of the user of the land
options.B: Transfers the ownership of the strip of land to the user
options.C: Cannot be withdrawn by the Railways under any circumstances
options.D: Is a bare permission to use the land for the specified purpose and creates no ownership or tenancy rights in favour of the user

e: Way-leave is only a bare permission to use railway land for a specified purpose, such as a crossing or pipeline; it creates no ownership, leasehold or tenancy rights in favour of the user.

q: On the expiry or termination of a licence of railway land, the licensee is required to:

options.A: Vacate the land and remove his structures at his own cost, handing back the land to the Railways
options.B: Sell his structures to the Railways at market value
options.C: Continue in occupation on payment of a penalty
options.D: Convert the licence into a lease as a matter of right

e: A licence creates no interest in the land, so on expiry or termination the licensee must vacate the land, remove his structures at his own cost and hand the land back to the Railways.

q: Consultants for railway projects and services are generally selected on the basis of:

options.A: The lowest financial bid alone
options.B: Nomination by the executing agency
options.C: Lottery among the empanelled firms
options.D: Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS), combining the technical and financial evaluations

e: Consultants are selected through Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS), which combines technical and financial evaluation, since the quality of professional services matters more than the lowest price alone.

q: A consultant engaged on a railway project is responsible for:

options.A: Executing the work with his own labour and materials
options.B: Supplying the stores required for the work
options.C: Financing the project on behalf of the Railways
options.D: Providing professional services such as design, advice and supervision, and not the physical execution of the work

e: A consultant renders professional services such as design, advice and supervision; the physical execution of the work is done by the executing agency or contractor, not by the consultant.

q: Work executed by a contractor which does not conform to the prescribed specifications may be:

options.A: Accepted with a nominal cut in all cases
options.B: Rejected by the Engineer, and the contractor required to remove and re-execute it at his own cost
options.C: Accepted after the Engineer pays a penalty to the Railways
options.D: Certified as satisfactory by the tender committee

e: Work not conforming to the prescribed specifications is liable to be rejected by the Engineer, and the contractor must remove and re-execute it at his own cost.

q: The strength of the concrete used in a work is checked by:

options.A: Testing of concrete cubes cast at the site and cured for the prescribed period
options.B: Weighing the concrete mix before placing
options.C: Visual inspection of the finished surface alone
options.D: Checking the contractor's purchase bills for cement

e: The strength of concrete is checked by testing cubes cast from the concrete placed at site and cured for the prescribed period, and testing them for compressive strength.

q: For important and major works, independent quality checks are got carried out through:

options.A: The contractor's own laboratory alone
options.B: A third-party inspection or quality audit agency, independent of the contractor
options.C: The finance branch of the Railway
options.D: The stores depot supplying the materials

e: For important works, quality is independently verified through a third-party inspection or quality audit agency, so that checking is not left to the contractor or the executing staff alone.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Inspection of the work by the Railway transfers the liability for defects in the work to the Railway.
options.B: The contractor remains responsible for the quality and soundness of the work, notwithstanding its inspection and acceptance by the Railway.
options.C: After inspection of the work, defects appearing in it are rectified at the cost of the Railways.
options.D: Acceptance of the final bill closes all claims of the Railways in respect of defective work.

e: Inspection and acceptance of the work by the Railway do not relieve the contractor of his responsibility for the quality and soundness of the work; liability for defects remains with him.

q: The fundamental principles of public buying laid down in the General Financial Rules emphasise:

options.A: Purchase from the nearest supplier in all cases
options.B: Preference to departmental production regardless of cost
options.C: Efficiency, economy, transparency, fair and equitable treatment of suppliers and promotion of competition
options.D: Purchase at the lowest price regardless of quality

e: The General Financial Rules lay down that public buying must observe efficiency, economy and transparency, ensure fair and equitable treatment of suppliers and promote competition.

q: Splitting up of a procurement or a work into smaller parts is objectionable mainly because:

options.A: It may be resorted to in order to avoid the sanction of a higher authority or the tender procedure applicable to the whole requirement
options.B: It increases the number of tender notices to be issued
options.C: It delays the payment of the contractor's bills
options.D: It is prohibited by the Indian Contract Act

e: Splitting a requirement is objectionable because it can be resorted to in order to keep each part within lower sanction limits or to avoid the tender procedure applicable to the whole requirement.

q: A tender which deviates materially from the conditions prescribed in the tender documents is treated as:

options.A: The lowest tender for the work
options.B: A conditional tender which must be accepted
options.C: A tender which can be accepted after negotiation
options.D: A non-responsive tender, liable to be rejected

e: A tender which deviates materially from the prescribed tender conditions is non-responsive, as it destroys the level playing field among tenderers, and is liable to be rejected.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Formation of a cartel or bid-rigging among tenderers is prohibited in public procurement.
2. Where cartel formation among tenderers is reasonably suspected, the tenders may be rejected and the matter dealt with in accordance with the procurement rules.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: cartel formation and bid-rigging among tenderers are prohibited in public procurement, and where collusion is reasonably suspected, the tenders may be rejected and action taken under the rules.

q: The eligibility (qualifying) criteria prescribed in works tender documents generally require the tenderer to demonstrate:

options.A: Ownership of land near the site of the work
options.B: Experience of having completed similar works and the prescribed minimum financial turnover
options.C: Registration as a company under the Companies Act in all cases
options.D: Employment of a minimum number of graduate engineers

e: Eligibility criteria establish the tenderer's capability, so tender documents generally require experience of having completed similar works and the prescribed minimum financial turnover.

q: A pre-bid conference in connection with a major or complex tender is held in order to:

options.A: Clarify the tender conditions and the scope of the work to the prospective tenderers before they submit their bids
options.B: Negotiate the rates with the tenderers
options.C: Open the technical bids in advance of the due date
options.D: Shortlist the contractors for a limited tender

e: A pre-bid conference allows prospective tenderers to seek clarifications on the tender conditions and the scope of the work before submitting bids, so that all offers rest on a common understanding.

q: After the tenders for a work are opened, the rates quoted by the various tenderers are tabulated item-wise in a document known as:

options.A: The deviation statement
options.B: The briefing note
options.C: The measurement abstract
options.D: The comparative statement

e: After the tenders are opened, the rates quoted by the various tenderers are tabulated item-wise in a comparative statement, which forms the basis for examination of the tenders.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The recommendations of a Tender Committee are recommendatory in nature, and the final decision on acceptance of a tender rests with the accepting authority.
2. The accepting authority is bound to accept the recommendation of the Tender Committee in every case.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: the Tender Committee's recommendations are recommendatory in nature. Statement 2 is wrong: the final decision rests with the accepting authority, which is not bound by the recommendation.

q: Acceptance of a tender other than the lowest (L1) tender:

options.A: Is never permissible under any circumstances
options.B: Is permissible only for reasons recorded in writing, with the concurrence of Finance
options.C: Requires the consent of the lowest tenderer
options.D: Can be ordered by the sectional officer without recording any reasons

e: Acceptance of a tender other than the lowest is an exception to the normal rule and is permissible only for reasons recorded in writing, with the concurrence of Finance.

q: The formation, validity and enforcement of contracts entered into by the Railways are governed in general by:

options.A: The Railways Act, 1989
options.B: The General Financial Rules
options.C: The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
options.D: The Indian Contract Act, 1872

e: Contracts entered into by the Railways, like other contracts, are governed in general by the Indian Contract Act, 1872, which lays down the law of offer, acceptance, consideration and breach.

q: The formal contract agreement executed after the issue of the Letter of Acceptance:

options.A: Replaces the tender documents entirely
options.B: Is required only in the case of deposit works
options.C: Incorporates the letter of acceptance, the accepted tender, the General Conditions of Contract and the special conditions, which together constitute the contract
options.D: Is executed between the contractor and the tender committee

e: The formal agreement incorporates the letter of acceptance, the accepted tender, the General Conditions of Contract and the special conditions, which together constitute the contract.

q: In a works contract, the stipulated period for completion of the work:

options.A: Is only an approximate indication for the guidance of the contractor
options.B: Is of the essence of the contract, and failure to complete within it exposes the contractor to levy of liquidated damages and termination
options.C: Can be extended by the contractor at his own discretion
options.D: Is decided after the work is physically completed

e: Time is of the essence of a works contract: the stipulated completion period binds the contractor, and failure to complete within it exposes him to liquidated damages and termination.

q: The Earnest Money Deposit of the successful tenderer is:

options.A: Adjusted towards the Security Deposit payable by him under the contract
options.B: Refunded to him immediately on the opening of tenders
options.C: Forfeited to the Railways in every case
options.D: Treated as earnings of the Railway

e: The earnest money deposit of the successful tenderer is retained by the Railways and adjusted towards the security deposit payable by him under the contract.

q: Which of the following is NOT an accepted mode of furnishing the Security Deposit/Performance Guarantee for a works contract?

options.A: Cash deposit
options.B: Bank guarantee from a scheduled bank
options.C: Deduction from the running bills of the contractor
options.D: A personal surety bond executed by another contractor

e: Security deposit and performance guarantee are accepted in forms such as cash, bank guarantee from a scheduled bank or deduction from running bills; a personal surety bond of another contractor is not an accepted mode.

q: Where the Security Deposit of a work is recovered through the contractor's bills:

options.A: The entire amount is deducted from the first running bill in all cases
options.B: A percentage is deducted from each running (on-account) bill until the full amount of the security deposit is recovered
options.C: The deduction is made only from the final bill of the work
options.D: The amount is recovered from the earnest money of the unsuccessful tenderers

e: Where the security deposit is recovered through bills, a percentage is deducted from each running (on-account) bill until the full amount of the security deposit is recovered.

q: On the failure of a contractor to fulfil his obligations under a contract, the Railway may:

options.A: Forfeit the earnest money deposits of all the tenderers
options.B: Recover damages only through a civil court
options.C: Invoke (encash) the bank guarantee furnished by the contractor towards the performance guarantee/security deposit, in accordance with the contract conditions
options.D: Stop all payments to all the contractors working in the division

e: On the contractor's failure to fulfil his obligations, the Railway may invoke and encash the bank guarantee furnished towards performance guarantee or security deposit, in accordance with the contract conditions.

q: Amounts found due from a contractor to the Railway under a contract may be recovered:

options.A: Only from the security deposit of that very contract
options.B: From any sums due or becoming due to the contractor under that contract or any other contract with the Railway
options.C: Only after obtaining a decree of a competent court
options.D: From the earnest money deposits of the unsuccessful tenderers

e: Amounts due from a contractor to the Railway may be recovered from any sums due or becoming due to him under that contract or any other contract with the Railway.

q: Short-closure (foreclosure) of a works contract means:

options.A: Termination of the contract on account of the contractor's default
options.B: Completion of the work ahead of the scheduled date
options.C: Suspension of the work during the monsoon period
options.D: Closing of the contract before its full scope is executed, with the approval of the competent authority, when the remaining work is no longer required

e: Short-closure means closing a contract before its full scope is executed, with the approval of the competent authority, when the remaining work is no longer required; it is not termination for default.

q: The Hindrance Register maintained in connection with a works contract records:

options.A: The names of the defaulting contractors of the division
options.B: The audit objections raised on the work
options.C: The hindrances encountered during execution, such as non-availability of site or of departmental materials, which are relevant while considering extension of the completion period
options.D: The daily attendance of the contractor's labour

e: The Hindrance Register records the hindrances encountered during execution, such as non-availability of site or departmental materials, which are relevant while considering extension of the completion period.

q: Under the General Conditions of Contract, the Engineer may order the suspension of the work, in whole or in part:

options.A: For reasons provided in the contract, such as the contractor's default or unsafe working, with the consequences regarding extension of time governed by the contract conditions
options.B: Only with the prior written permission of the contractor
options.C: Only after the expiry of the stipulated completion period
options.D: Only on the directions of the tender committee

e: Under the General Conditions of Contract, the Engineer may order suspension of the work for reasons provided in the contract, such as the contractor's default or unsafe working, with time consequences governed by the contract.

q: On the award of a work, the contractor is required to submit:

options.A: A list of his labourers with their home addresses
options.B: A detailed programme of execution, such as a bar chart, showing how he proposes to complete the work within the stipulated period
options.C: The completion report of the work
options.D: A bank guarantee equal to the full contract value

e: On award of a work, the contractor submits a detailed programme of execution, such as a bar chart, showing how he proposes to complete the work within the stipulated period.

q: Until a completed work is taken over by the Railway, the responsibility for the care, custody and protection of the work rests with:

options.A: The tender committee
options.B: The Accounts office
options.C: The department which will use the asset
options.D: The contractor

e: Until a completed work is taken over by the Railway, the responsibility for the care, custody and protection of the work rests with the contractor.

q: After a work is completed and the completion certificate is issued, the asset is:

options.A: Handed over to the contractor for permanent maintenance
options.B: Kept with the construction organisation indefinitely
options.C: Handed over to the department responsible for its use and maintenance, which thereafter maintains it
options.D: Transferred to the Railway Board

e: After completion and issue of the completion certificate, the asset is handed over to the department responsible for its use and maintenance, which thereafter maintains it.

q: 'Completion drawings' of a work are:

options.A: Drawings showing the work as actually executed, prepared on completion of the work
options.B: The drawings attached to the tender documents
options.C: The survey drawings prepared before the estimate is framed
options.D: The drawings prepared by the contractor for fabrication of materials

e: Completion drawings are drawings showing the work as actually executed, prepared on completion of the work, recording all deviations from the original drawings.

q: Instructions issued to the contractor at the site of a work by the Engineer or his representative are recorded in:

options.A: The Contractor's Ledger
options.B: The Site Order Book maintained at the site of the work
options.C: The Works Register
options.D: The tender notice

e: Instructions issued to the contractor at the site by the Engineer or his representative are recorded in the Site Order Book maintained at the site of the work.

q: A Measurement Book issued for recording measurements of works:

options.A: Is an ordinary notebook maintained by the contractor
options.B: Contains blank pages which can be replaced when filled
options.C: Need not be preserved after the work is completed
options.D: Has its pages consecutively (machine) numbered and is treated as an important accountable record

e: A Measurement Book has its pages consecutively machine-numbered and is treated as an important accountable record, so that no page can be inserted, removed or replaced.

q: If an entry recorded in a Measurement Book requires correction:

options.A: The original entry should be erased and rewritten
options.B: The entry should be overwritten with the correct figures
options.C: The entry should be corrected by striking it out, with the correction attested by the initials and date of the official making it
options.D: The page containing the entry should be torn out of the book

e: A wrong entry in a Measurement Book is corrected by striking it out, keeping it legible, and writing the correction, attested by the initials and date of the official making it; erasure or overwriting is not permitted.

q: Before a contractor's on-account or final bill is prepared, the Abstract of Measurements is prepared in order to:

options.A: Summarise, item-wise, the quantities of work measured in the Measurement Book on which the bill is based
options.B: Record the hindrances met during the execution of the work
options.C: Tabulate the rates quoted by all the tenderers
options.D: Work out the departmental charges of the work

e: The Abstract of Measurements summarises, item-wise, the quantities of work measured in the Measurement Book, and the contractor's on-account or final bill is prepared on its basis.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Where the delay in completion of a work is attributable to the contractor, extension of time may be granted with levy of liquidated damages for the period of delay so attributable.
2. Where the delay is due to causes beyond the control of the contractor, extension of time is granted without levy of liquidated damages.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: extension for delay attributable to the contractor is granted with levy of liquidated damages, while delay due to causes beyond the contractor's control is granted extension without liquidated damages.

q: Liquidated damages stipulated in a works contract are best described as:

options.A: A penalty imposed at the discretion of the Engineer
options.B: A genuine pre-estimate, agreed in the contract, of the loss likely to be suffered by the Railway on account of delayed completion
options.C: The profit element of the contract, recovered back from the contractor
options.D: A fine imposed under the Railways Act, 1989

e: Liquidated damages are a genuine pre-estimate, agreed in the contract, of the loss likely to be suffered by the Railway on account of delayed completion; they are not a penalty or a fine.

q: Serviceable materials released from an asset which is dismantled or replaced are:

options.A: Handed over to the contractor as his property
options.B: Sold as scrap in every case
options.C: Retained at the site without any accountal
options.D: Taken back into stores stock, and their value credited to the work/head of account bearing the cost of the replacement

e: Serviceable materials released from a dismantled or replaced asset remain Railway property; they are taken back into stores stock and their value credited to the work or head bearing the cost of the replacement.

q: The 'throw-forward' of the Works Programme represents:

options.A: The number of works sanctioned during the year
options.B: The expenditure incurred on works during the previous year
options.C: The savings anticipated in the works budget
options.D: The total balance cost of sanctioned works in progress which remains to be spent in the coming years

e: The throw-forward of the Works Programme represents the total balance cost of sanctioned works in progress which remains to be spent in the coming years.

q: In connection with surveys for new railway lines, RETS stands for:

options.A: Reconnaissance Engineering-cum-Traffic Survey
options.B: Railway Engineering and Track Survey
options.C: Regional Estimate and Traffic Statement
options.D: Reconnaissance Estimate for Track Strengthening

e: RETS stands for Reconnaissance Engineering-cum-Traffic Survey, the first-stage survey for a new line combining a preliminary engineering examination with an assessment of the traffic prospects.

q: A traffic survey carried out for a proposed new railway line primarily assesses:

options.A: The soil conditions along the proposed alignment
options.B: The availability of construction materials near the alignment
options.C: The traffic likely to be carried and the earnings expected, so as to judge the remunerativeness of the proposal
options.D: The requirement of staff for working the new line

e: A traffic survey for a proposed new line primarily assesses the traffic likely to be carried and the earnings expected, so as to judge the remunerativeness of the proposal.

q: Extra Budgetary Resources (Institutional Finance) — EBR(IF) — for railway projects are raised mainly:

options.A: From the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) by way of market borrowings
options.C: From the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: By levy of a cess on passengers

e: Extra Budgetary Resources (Institutional Finance) are raised mainly through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) by way of market borrowings, outside the budgetary support.
